learning_results:
The unified recurrent controller learned useful current and robot actions, but **it did not qualify for deployment**. Its slightly better worst peak on the 700-case nominal grid did not transfer reliably to fresh conditions or prolonged motion. The deterministic controller remains the stronger prototype starting point; even that controller needs more margin and timing verification.

**Question.** Can one history-based policy control the complete flange while maintaining workpiece-normal force within ±0.5 N and managing delayed robot recentering? The experiment used one shared, two-layer, 32-state Puffer minGRU with causal force, acceleration, relative position, identified parameters and already-issued robot commands. It received no future bump profile. Its two outputs commanded coil current and robot correction through the unchanged native current driver, stability gate, delay and limits. There was no dynamic PI force controller underneath the learned current action.

**Training and selection.** Physics-informed initialization supplied force balance and causal filter features. Whole-episode evolutionary rewards adjusted successive compact parameter sets, including recurrent readouts; this was not teacher-action imitation or learning from a blank network. The stored network contains 8,101 trainable parameters, while individual evolutionary stages optimized 12, 28, 55, 41 or 37 degrees of freedom. These counts must not be confused.

The evolutionary lane completed 124 generations on the earlier sensor configuration and one generation after the budget-sensor change: **17,728 training episodes and 480,771,873 actor decisions**. The earlier stage executed 20,104 episodes including its selection and audit runs, plus 368 physics-initialization comparisons and 38 implementation checks; 21 evolutionary training episodes and three initialization comparisons physically failed. These counts exclude the separately recorded PPO experiments. The budget stage executed 616 scored episodes: 424 evolutionary training/selection/audit episodes, 136 bootstrap comparisons and 56 paired transfer-screen episodes. Five physical failures occurred in the latter two groups; the single budget evolutionary generation had none. Recovery replays remain separate from optimization counts.

The final budget winner was the reward-selected `history_0p5` attenuation of previously evolved current-history weights. It did **not** receive the final budget evolutionary update. Its direct budget evidence before locking was **20 training cases plus all 28 selection cases**, all passing, with 0.454059 N selection worst error. Other candidates' 84-case audits do not belong to this checkpoint. The checkpoint was frozen before final testing, and neither weights nor selection were changed after seeing those results.

![Development convergence; the earlier stages use the faster reference sensing chain.](development_convergence.svg)

**Final results.** All force scores include startup and every native integration sample. A pass requires completing the recording without a physical stop while remaining within ±0.5 N. The ±7.5 mm travel band is reported separately as the user's preferred operating region; crossing it is different from reaching the physical ±12.5 mm stop.

| Final cohort | Deterministic passes; worst force error | Learned passes; worst force error | Entire recording inside ±7.5 mm, deterministic / learned |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 700 nominal grid cases | 700/700; 0.428526 N | 700/700; 0.418410 N | 700/700 / 700/700 |
| 32 fresh cases | 32/32; 0.483324 N | 30/32; 0.678521 N | 32/32 / 32/32 |
| Four 30 s cases | 4/4; 0.492243 N | 3/4; 0.489666 N before termination | 2/4 / 2/4 |

These are **1,472 scored recordings (736 baseline/policy pairs) and 1,005,340,754 native sample points**. Eight additional retained replay recordings are excluded from those qualification counts. The 700-case nominal grid checks parameter coverage; it does not replace the distinct fresh-condition and long-duration tests.

The nominal peak improvement was only 0.010116 N. Mean per-recording RMS error increased from 0.016068 N to 0.040781 N. On fresh cases it increased from 0.027376 N to 0.048349 N. Fresh case 86, at 33 N, S=1.1 kg and 50°, reached 0.678521 N; case 94 also exceeded the limit at 0.501417 N. Neither failure involved contact loss or a travel stop.

![Paired fresh-case force results.](rl_3h_fresh_pairs.svg)
![The worst fresh force recording.](rl_3h_worst_force.svg)
![The separate 700-case nominal grid.](rl_3h_nominal_grid.svg)

In the long 50 N, S=2 kg, 90° case, the learned controller reached the travel stop at **19.13094 s**. Its force remained below 0.5 N until termination, which does not make the recording a pass. The deterministic controller completed all four long recordings but exceeded the preferred travel band in two, reaching 9.028 mm from center. Its worst force reserve was just **0.007757 N**. Neither result supports a claim of comfortable long-duration robustness. There were no software rejections or robot request-clock/gate violations in the final cohorts; obeying the gate alone does not guarantee sufficient recentering.

![Robot travel relative to the preferred band.](rl_3h_robot_travel.svg)
![The learned controller's long-run physical stop.](rl_3h_long_stop.svg)

**Performance limits.** Two additional locked-policy development screens each ran the same 28 cases with both controllers: 112 scored episodes and 3,658,783 actor decisions, with two recovery replays counted separately. They did not alter the final winner.

| Budget-chain development condition | Deterministic passes; worst error | Learned passes; worst error |
|---|---:|---:|
| 50 µs current response, declared sensing timing | 28/28; 0.463682 N | 28/28; 0.454059 N |
| 100 µs current response | 28/28; 0.493979 N | 26/28; 0.640529 N |
| 50 µs current response plus known, matched 50 µs sensing delay | 26/28; 0.513855 N | 15/28; 1.129700 N |

The learned policy also suffered one physical stop with the slower current response and two with added sensing delay. The 100 µs condition's worst force case had **no voltage clipping**, so a higher supply voltage at unchanged current-loop tuning cannot explain away that failure. Added latency remained harmful even when known and matched in identification. These experiments identify current-loop response and synchronized sensor phase as concrete constraints; voltage headroom is only one part of the problem.

![Recorded drive effort and clipping.](rl_3h_drive.svg)
![Paired budget current-response and latency limits.](budget_response_limits.svg)
learning_recommendation:
**Recommendation.** Build the budget prototype around the deterministic measured-inertia controller, using the voice coil, upper rigid link and lower opposed spring pair. Retain approximately 19.7 kN/m combined stiffness and 60 N·s/m external damping, and identify the assembled mechanics for each tool. The approximate spring packing remains comfortably within the 100 mm spring-only condition.

Use the budget accelerometer/ADC chain as a **conditional prototype target**: ADXL354-class acceleration sensing, ADS131M08 acquisition at 30 ksample/s, matched 1.9 kHz response envelopes, synchronized force/acceleration measurements and a 10 kHz controller. Target the tested 50 µs current response with at least 32 V usable bipolar output from the proposed 36 V supply. Verify these response and timing figures on the assembled hardware, including filtering, ADC delay, driver phase, calibration and noise; nominal sample rate alone is insufficient.

Before sanding trials, improve and validate sustained robot recentering and establish more force margin than the 0.007757 N long-case reserve. Check thermal operation and structural modes under real sanding vibration. Keep the neural policy as a reproducible research candidate with its failures intact. **Do not deploy it as the flange controller on the evidence obtained here.**
